risks.claim: The No Surprises Act IDR framework is in regulatory flux: the Fifth Circuit en banc vacated the ghost-rates QPA methodology on August 11, 2026, and new HHS rules have not yet been promulgated, creating uncertainty over future out-of-network reimbursement levels that drive a large share of hospital revenue.

HHS, No. 23-40605, vacating key portions of the July 2021 interim final rule (July 2021 Rule) promulgated by the Departments of Health and Human Services, Labor, and Treasury (Departments).

The court upheld the district court's vacatur of the July 2021 rule, directing the Departments to exercise their enforcement discretion to allow insurers to continue using their existing QPAs until new QPAs are calculated in accordance with new rules promulgated by the Departments consistent with the NSA.
We cannot predict how such final opinion will affect the QPA calculation or the opinion's impact on out-of-network payments awarded in the IDR process.

risks.claim: HaloMD, Nutex's exclusive IDR vendor handling 50-60% of its medical claims, faces pending insurer lawsuits alleging fraudulent IDR submissions; adverse outcomes or a short-seller narrative could impair Nutex's IDR revenue stream and reputation.
quotes: Since May 2024, HaloMD has handled, on an exclusive basis, all out-of-network claims made by Nutex that are eligible for arbitration under federal and state 'no surprise' laws. During the year ended December 31, 2025, HaloMD submitted approximately 50-60% of the Company's medical claims through the IDR process.
Pending or future litigation against HaloMD could materially adversely impact the revenues we expect to receive from the medical claims submitted on our behalf by HaloMD.

During 2026, federal district courts in several jurisdictions have granted the defendants' motions to dismiss many of these lawsuits, primarily on the grounds that the NSA bars judicial review of IDR determinations except for certain narrow exceptions permitted under the Federal Arbitration Act that were not met.

risks.basis: Stated in P6 (8-K earnings release with revenue comparison and explanation) and P3 (10-K MD&A explaining the 2024 IDR estimation change)
risks.claim: Total revenue declined 6.3% in H1 2026 versus H1 2025 and 13.6% in Q2 2026 versus Q2 2025, as the one-time IDR estimation improvement that drove the 2024-2025 revenue surge has normalized, raising the question of whether the prior growth trajectory is sustainable.
quotes: Total revenue decreased 6.3% to $427.2 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to $455.8 million for the same period in 2025, while revenue at same hospitals decreased 6.0%.
Total revenue decreased 13.6% to $210.8 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to $244.0 million for the same period in 2025, while revenue at same hospitals, decreased 12.1%.
Most of the revenue decrease in 2026 compared to 2025 is due to the positive results from the early stage improvement in the IDR process that were realized in the first half of 2025.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K risk factors on CEO conflicts) and P1 (10-K Business section describing the entity structure)
risks.claim: Chairman and CEO Dr. Vo has conflicts of interest as co-owner of real estate entities that lease hospital facilities to the company and as a recipient of earn-out shares, potentially transferring value from public stockholders to related parties.
quotes: In his capacity as the co-owner of the real estate entities that lease the land and buildings to our hospital facilities, Dr. Vo, our Chairman, CEO and major stockholder, may have conflicts of interest with the Company and its public stockholders.
Many of these entities are owned in part, and in some cases controlled, by our Chairman and Chief Executive Officer.
We have no ownership interest in any of the Physician LLCs and have a 51% interest in one of the Real Estate Entities, but provide back office accounting for each.

we estimate, based on current expectations, to issue approximately 88,500 additional shares, or 1.2% of our outstanding shares as of December 31, 2025.

risks.basis: Stated in P10 (8-K on the HaloMD amendment) and P6 (8-K earnings release quantifying the $52.3 million impact)
risks.claim: The company's exclusive IDR vendor relationship with HaloMD was amended effective June 30, 2026 to transition to a pay-on-collected fee basis and give Nutex the right to perform dispute resolution in-house for future facilities, reducing single-vendor dependency but creating transition risk.
quotes: Effective June 30, 2026, Nutex Health Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company"), on July 15, 2026, entered into a First Amendment (the "Amendment") to that certain Payment Dispute Resolution Services Agreement, dated as of May 1, 2024 (the "Agreement"), by and between the Company and HaloMD, L.L.C.

provides the Company the right to perform dispute resolution services either in-house or through the engagement of another third-party vendor or service provider with respect to certain future hospital facilities, and (v) extends the initial term of the Agreement through December 31, 2029, subject to automatic one-year renewals.
The cumulative impact from these two key changes directly reduced the contract services expenses for the second quarter and six months ended 2026 period by $52.3 million.
